entries.snippet: Consumer prices in July were up 3.4% from a year ago — a smaller annual increase than in May or June. The news makes it less likely the Fed will feel the need to raise interest rates in September.

entries.title: Earthquake response strains Colombia's new government and rescuers as they race against the clock
entries.snippet: Tons of aid from regional partners began to roll into Colombia on Wednesday, as the search for survivors in the rubble of powerful earthquake grew more desperate after the temblor razed buildings, buckled roads and crushed cars.

entries.snippet: The Department of Justice has charged nearly a dozen people with participating in a multimillion-dollar scheme to help hundreds of Chinese nationals fraudulently obtain green cards through sham marriages to U.S. citizens, officials said Wednesday.

entries.snippet: At a time when many Americans remain stressed about affordability, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has declared that the U.S. economy is no longer in a "K shape," a term used to describe increasing financial inequality between high- and low-income households.

entries.title: 3 states are set to hold executions on the same day, a first in the US since 2010
entries.snippet: Tennessee, Alabama and Oklahoma plan to execute inmates Thursday in what would be the first time in nearly 16 years that three people are put to death on the same day in the United States.

entries.title: PHOTOS: Millions gather to watch Europe's first total solar eclipse in decades
entries.snippet: Millions of people crowded cloudless cities and towns in Spain on Wednesday in search of the best views of a total solar eclipse, when the alignment of the sun, moon and Earth will briefly plunge parts of the planet into darkness.

entries.title: AP report: ICE plans to give its officers gloves that can deliver painful electric shocks

entries.title: Lindsay Clancy trial turns focus to medications prescribed before she killed her children

entries.title: Peggy Flanagan wins Senate primary in Minnesota, notching another victory for progressive Democrats
entries.snippet: Flanagan defeated centrist Rep. Angie Craig with a pledge to fight the influence of corporations and confront Republican President Donald Trump.

entries.title: Sen. Darline Graham, Rep. Ralph Norman advance to GOP runoff in South Carolina
entries.snippet: A first-time candidate who was always close to her brother's political orbit, Darline Graham overcame skepticism about her lack of experience in her campaign to replace him, as she moved forward Tuesday as the top vote-getter to runner-up Norman.

entries.title: David Crowley wins Democratic primary for Wisconsin governor over Francesca Hong
entries.snippet: Crowley narrowly defeated democratic socialist Hong, who was hoping to ride the wave of recent victories by progressive candidates, including Abdul El-Sayed in neighboring Michigan's U.S. Senate race last week.

entries.snippet: News, Analysis and Service from Germany and Europe - in 30 Languages

entries.title: Eurovision bars countries at war from hosting
entries.snippet: A Eurovision victory will no longer guarantee hosting rights if war or a wider security crisis affects the winning country. The change could have particular significance for recent high-flyers Ukraine and Israel.

entries.title: Russia: Why is the Yabloko party barred from the elections?
entries.snippet: Russia's supreme court has banned the anti-war opposition party Yabloko from September's parliamentary elections. What does this mean for the election campaign, opponents of the war and for the political mood in Russia?

entries.title: 25 years Ohrid Agreement: Is N. Macedonia's peace holding?
entries.snippet: A quarter of a century after the Ohrid Framework Agreement ended North Macedonia's 2001 conflict, analysts warn that peace between ethnic communities remains fragile.

entries.title: No oil, no salary: Iraqi state employees are feeling the crunch of the Hormuz blockade
entries.snippet: Because of the blockage of the Strait of Hormuz, Iraq cannot export enough oil to fund the country's huge public sector. Protests have already started. Will the Iran war destabilize Iraq again?

entries.title: Mozart tribute ends on sour note after mass figurine theft
entries.snippet: A playful tribute to Mozart has turned into a whodunit after 210 gold-colored figures disappeared from one of Austria's busiest tourist spots. The mass theft forced organizers to end the outdoor display early.

entries.title: Unconstitutional? German intelligence to receive more powers
entries.snippet: German intelligence agencies have been calling for more powers in the fight against cyberattacks, terrorism and extremism. Now the government has given the go. Critics warn that red lines are being crossed.

entries.title: Eritrea: An emerging key player in the geopolitical gamble at the Horn
entries.snippet: Amid growing tensions and security risks at the Horn of Africa, Eritrea, with its strategically important coastal points on the Red Sea and a perceived lack of conflict, is emerging as important player in the region.

entries.title: Italy: Etna eruption in Sicily halts Catania flights
entries.snippet: Sicily's Catania airport has suspended flights again as Mount Etna continues to spew lava and volcanic ash. The eruption has disrupted travel during the peak summer holiday season.

entries.title: Gulf states scramble for Strait of Hormuz alternative
entries.snippet: Saudi Arabia has redirected oil exports away from the Strait of Hormuz, but most Gulf producers still lack a reliable backup option to the world's most important energy choke point.

entries.title: India: Data centers boom as water supply runs low
entries.snippet: More than half of India's data centers are in regions that are already water-stressed ― and the country is racing to build more.

entries.title: Short on US Patriot missiles, Ukraine looks for alternatives
entries.snippet: Russia is putting pressure on Ukraine with ballistic missiles, but Kyiv is short of Patriot interceptors. Domestic production and European alternatives take time. Can Kyiv realistically reduce its dependence on the US?

entries.title: Europe braces for next heat wave
entries.snippet: More than half the continent, including much of Germany, is set for a third wave of extreme heat this summer. The prolonged hot weather has significantly worsened wildfires and drought conditions across Europe.

entries.title: Germany news: Cabinet approves intelligence service reforms
entries.snippet: Germany's domestic and foreign intelligence services are to get greater powers to deal with hybrid threats. Meanwhile, transport ministers are meeting to find solutions to increasingly low river levels. DW has more.

entries.title: EU waste packaging rules: Why small businesses are worried
entries.snippet: The EU has introduced new rules targeting packaging waste and "forever chemicals." Although the changes will be phased in slowly, some small sellers have already paused shipments due to the additional red tape.

entries.title: AI helping create popular mobile sports games
entries.snippet: After the World Cup and before the domestic season, many fans still crave more football. Amateur coders are helping to fill this gap.

entries.title: Zambia's 2026 election: Key issues to watch
entries.snippet: Economic recovery, youth turnout, women's representation and judicial independence are among the issues shaping Zambia's vote on Thursday.

entries.title: Solar eclipse: What to look forward to
entries.snippet: The last solar eclipse visible from the European mainland was in 1999. Here's what to expect, and how to prepare for this rare occasion.

entries.title: India news: IndiGo engine failure triggers airport emergency
entries.snippet: Chennai airport declared full emergency after an IndiGo flight suffered an engine failure, hours after reports that an Air India pilot involved in an on-air incident last week tested positive in a drug test.

entries.title: Pakistan says 3 nationals killed in Houthi Red Sea attack
entries.snippet: Pakistan's foreign minister has said Islamabad "strongly condemns" Houthi attacks on commercial vessels while offering condolences to the families of the dead.
